Mox v0.7.0 brings the hub, editor, and add flow into one terminal workspace,
with clearer session states and better protection for unsaved work.

### Terminal UI

- Hub, editor, and add share a session rail, work area, and action/status rows.
  Adding a session from the editor keeps the rail and selection in place.
- Running, stopped, tmux-only, and draft states have text labels. Essential
  text follows your terminal foreground in light, dark, and no-color modes.
- Narrow terminals use Tab to switch areas. Long forms and YAML reviews scroll
  within the viewport; selection and input survive resizing.
- Shortcuts reflect the current state. `?` shows contextual help outside text
  input; `/` and `?` remain literal characters inside text fields.
- Ctrl+C protects unsaved drafts and active input. Backtracking in add retains
  entered values, commands, and the broadcast choice. In the editor, `u` opens
  save/discard/stay; `D` asks before discarding a new unsaved session.

### Reliability

- Config loading, editing, and importing reject additional YAML documents
  instead of silently dropping them. Import validates the resulting config
  before saving.
- Recents history and `mox init --force` use atomic replacement; forced init
  preserves symlinked config paths.
- `--print` quotes shell metacharacters so pasted commands retain their arguments.
- Added windows target exact session names, avoiding tmux prefix matches.
- Hub key replay stops after quitting, and validation reports layouts in a
  consistent order.

### Install or update

Download the archive for your OS and architecture below and verify it against
`checksums.txt`, or build the tagged version with Go 1.25 or newer:

```sh
go install github.com/bthall/mox/cmd/mox@v0.7.0
```

Runtime requires tmux 3.1 or newer. Existing single-document configurations
continue to work, and updating the binary does not require restarting tmux.
